prior_notes.title: Community atlas working notebook
prior_notes.body:
# Community atlas working notebook

This notebook accumulated the decisions, checks and loose ends from preparation of the community atlas. It remains the place people scan for the state of the whole effort.

## Working inventory

| Area | Current state | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route exports | The export trial compares the visitor and maintenance editions. | Review the trial result. |
| Index layout | Place entries in two columns. Keep cross-references beside the entry that needs them. | Check the last spread. |
| Contributor introductions | New contributors receive the short map-reading example before editing a route description. | Add the next introduction slot. |
| Event programme | The walk-through happens before the question session. Keep the final half hour free for corrections. | Confirm the order on the printed programme. |
| Place labels | Labels use the full approved place name on first mention and the short form afterward. | Reconcile the label sheet with the index. |
| Illustration captions | Captions explain what the drawing shows rather than restating its title. | Review the remaining captions. |
| Archive bundle | Preserve the editable map, exported editions and change summary together for each edition. | Check that the edition identifier matches. |
| Feedback intake | Collect route corrections separately from comments on the publication layout. | Read the two lists before the next editing meeting. |
| Reading session | Read route descriptions aloud before finalizing punctuation. | Arrange the next reading order. |
| Print proof | A proof reader checks that symbols remain legible when the page is reduced. | Compare the final spread at its printed size. |

## Recent editorial notes

The index discussion settled column layout. It did not change route geometry. The contributor example concerns how descriptions are edited; it does not define which routes belong in an edition.

The publication archive is an edition record. It should preserve what was actually released even when a later edition changes a route. Corrections received after release belong to the next edition unless an existing release needs an explicit correction notice.

## Programme notes

The walk-through introduces the atlas as a whole. The question session follows it because readers can then refer to a concrete route. The open correction period is for gathering feedback, not for deciding the map style during the event.

The first print proof exposed a caption that repeated its heading. That caption needs a description of the drawing instead. This is separate from the symbol-size check on the reduced spread.

prior_notes.title: Atlas route export contract
prior_notes.body:
# Atlas route export contract

This note defines which route geometry each edition includes and how an export implements that choice.

## Current rule

The visitor edition and maintenance edition currently reuse one route layer. The visitor style hides access gates and staff-only shortcuts. The maintenance style shows the full route layer.

## Unresolved check

The export trial must establish whether style-only hiding remains reliable when someone changes the visitor style. The trial has not yet settled this question.

## Scope

This contract covers route inclusion and the public or maintenance export boundary. Index layout, captions, contributor introductions and event planning have their own purposes.

prior_notes.title: Trail sign review workflow
prior_notes.body:
# Trail sign review workflow

This workflow covers the text and direction arrows on trail signs before publication.

## Review

The first reviewer checks arrow directions against the map. The second reviewer checks destination names, but the reference used for that check has not yet been specified. Both reviewers record any correction on the draft.

## Publication

After both reviewers complete their checks, the editor resolves recorded corrections. The editor then publishes the sign text. A later change returns through the same review before publication.

prior_notes.title: Transcription batch handoff protocol
prior_notes.body:
# Transcription batch handoff protocol

This protocol follows one batch of captured leaves from intake through transcription and shift handoff. The manifest, text and review state travel together because the next shift must reconstruct the exact order and see which decisions remain open.

## Batch identity and order

Assign the batch its edition identifier and sequence range before transcription begins. Use the capture sequence as the ordering authority. A printed page number helps a reader identify a leaf, but it does not replace the capture sequence.

Record an unnumbered leaf in its capture position. Put the phrase that begins that leaf in the manifest so that a reviewer can distinguish it from an empty gap. Keep a blank leaf in the sequence and mark it as blank; do not silently remove it.

## Manifest fields

| Field | Meaning | Handoff check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edition | The edition to which the batch belongs. | It matches the text and review sheet. |
| Capture sequence | The leaf's order in this captured batch. | Every captured leaf has one position. |
| Printed page number | The number visible on the leaf, if present. | A missing number remains explicitly absent. |
| Opening phrase | The first readable words on the leaf. | It distinguishes an unnumbered leaf. |
| Text state | Whether the leaf awaits transcription, review or resolution. | The next shift can identify the next useful action. |
| Open question | The text or order issue that still needs a decision. | It points to the leaf and the uncertain passage. |
| Review result | The result of comparing the transcription with the leaf. | It records corrections without pretending an open question is settled. |

## Work through the batch

| Stage | Action | Result carried forward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intake | Compare the captured leaves with the manifest. | Each leaf has a place in the capture sequence. |
| First pass | Transcribe each leaf in capture order. | Text remains associated with its leaf. |
| Unclear text | Preserve the readable text and mark the uncertain passage. | The question stays visible to the next reviewer. |
| Review pass | Compare the transcription against the captured leaf. | Corrections and unresolved passages remain distinct. |
| Order check | Compare leaf transitions with the manifest. | A missing or duplicated position becomes an open question. |
| Shift handoff | Assemble the manifest, current text and review sheet. | The next shift can continue without guessing. |

## Exceptions

An unnumbered leaf keeps its capture position and opening phrase. A blank leaf stays in the manifest. If a leaf is unreadable, record that state and continue with the next captured leaf; do not fill the gap from context.

If a transition appears inconsistent, leave the capture sequence intact and record the question for review. Do not silently reorder leaves based only on how the sentences sound. The protocol does not yet state a specific procedure for two distinct leaves that share one printed page number.

## Complete the handoff

Read the manifest from the first capture position to the last. Check that every position still has a leaf or an explicit unresolved state. Compare edition and sequence identifiers across the manifest, text and review sheet.

At shift end, write a short handoff summary that identifies the next incomplete position and any open questions. A complete batch can still contain an unresolved reading if that reading is marked and assigned for review. Do not describe the batch as fully resolved merely because every leaf has a transcription.

The incoming shift starts with the manifest, then opens the corresponding text and review sheet. It should be possible to distinguish a leaf awaiting review from one that was reviewed and still needs a decision.

prior_notes.title: Transcription reading session format
prior_notes.body:
# Transcription reading session format

A reading session compares the sound of a completed passage with its intended punctuation. Readers mark difficult phrasing for the editor.

The session does not decide captured leaf order or replace the batch handoff checks.
